mechanism_narrative: A quarterly increase in GDPC1, indicating strengthening economic demand, boosts consumer and business confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of quarters with positive GDPC1 growth.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, signaling a tightening monetary cycle, equity valuations are negatively impacted, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive in > 40% of tightening cycles with FEDFUNDS above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Jointly, when UNRATE falls below 4% and PAYEMS shows a 3-month increase, indicating a strong labor market, S&P 500 forward returns are positively impacted over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 55% of instances meeting the joint labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in INDPRO, signaling improved industrial production, positively influences S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing cycles with positive INDPRO growth are not significantly higher than in neutral cycles (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in HOUST, indicating a strong housing market, supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as it reflects overall economic health.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this mechanism remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds a 3-month average of 325, indicating rising inflation, and FEDFUNDS is above 4%, the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated monetary tightening.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 45% of instances meeting the joint inflation and interest rate conditions.

mechanism_narrative: Always, the level of UNRATE, as a standalone indicator of labor market conditions, has a positive influence on S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, with lower rates indicating stronger markets.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no significant correlation with UNRATE levels over a 2-year window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, when RSAFS shows a monthly increase, indicating increased retail sales, S&P 500 forward returns are positively impacted over the next 20 trading days, reflecting strong consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in late-cycle expansions with positive RSAFS growth are not significantly higher than in early-cycle expansions (t-test p > 0.05).
